title: Relative ampleness is open on the base
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. If $x\in X$ and the restriction $\mathcal M|_{Y_x}$ to the fibre [def-pc-fibre-product] is ample in the absolute sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ in $X$ such that $f^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact and $\mathcal M|_{f^{-1}(U)}$ is ample on every inverse image of an affine open of $U$ (that is, it is relatively ample over $U$ in the stated sense).

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $X^0$ of $x$. The restricted morphism $Y^0=f^{-1}(X^0)\to X^0$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Its fibre over $x$ and the restricted invertible module give the original fibre and module. It suffices to produce the required open $U\subseteq X^0$, since every affine open of $U$ and its inverse image are the same in the original schemes. Rename this restriction $f:Y\to X$. The affine base $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].

source.place: Tag 0D2S, first sentence of proof; Tag 01W4 for proper base change.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-limit-noetherian] to obtain a small nonempty directed system $f_i:Y_i\to X_i$ with affine transitions, proper $f_i$, affine $X_i$ of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and limits $Y$ and $X$ with projections $a_i:Y\to Y_i$, $b_i:X\to X_i$ satisfying $f_i a_i=b_i f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], each $X_i$ is Noetherian and each $Y_i$ is Noetherian, since proper means finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. In particular $Y_i$ is quasi-compact; it is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated].

source.place: Tag 0D2S, approximation paragraph, invoking Limits Tag 0A0P; Tags 01T6 and 01OY for the stage hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-invertible-affine-limit-descent] to $(Y_i)$ and $\mathcal M$ to obtain $i_0$, an invertible module $M_0$ on $Y_{i_0}$, and $a_{i_0}^*M_0\cong\mathcal M$. For $i\geq i_0$ define $M_i=q_{i i_0}^*M_0$. These modules are invertible, their further pullbacks agree with the $M_j$, and $a_i^*M_i\cong\mathcal M$, by the invertible-pullback and composition clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. Work on the directed tail $i\geq i_0$. It retains the same limits: for a cone on the tail, its component at an arbitrary $i$ is the component at any $j\geq i,i_0$ followed by the transition to $i$; the cone identities and a common upper bound show independence of $j$. This extends cones uniquely and proves the required universal properties.

source.place: Tag 0D2S, descent of the invertible modules via Limits Tag 0B8W.

proof.text: Put $x_i=b_i(x)$ and $F_i=(Y_i)_{x_i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-residue-field], $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is the compatible limit of the $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x_i)$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-limit-fibre-products] identifies $Y_x$ with $\varprojlim F_i$ and gives affine transition maps on the $F_i$. Each $F_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x_i)$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence of finite type and separated. Consequently each $F_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. The restriction of $M_0$ to $F_{i_0}$ pulls back to $M_i|_{F_i}$ and to $\mathcal M|_{Y_x}$, by the commuting fibre squares and the pullback composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor].

source.place: Tag 0D2S, residue-field colimit and the application of Limits Tag 09MT; Limits Tag 0CUG and lemma-limit-fibre-product.

proof.text: The hypothesis makes $\mathcal M|_{Y_x}$ ample. The pullback isomorphism of Step 4 and [lem-sc-ample-iso] therefore satisfy the hypothesis of [lem-trf-ample-affine-limit-descent] for the system $(F_i)$ and $M_0|_{F_{i_0}}$. Obtain $i\geq i_0$ such that $M_i|_{F_i}$ is ample. The base $X_i$ is Noetherian by Step 2 and $f_i$ is proper, so [lem-trf-noetherian-fibre-ample-neighbourhood] gives an affine open neighbourhood $V_i$ of $x_i$ with $M_i|_{f_i^{-1}(V_i)}$ ample in the absolute sense.

source.place: Tag 0D2S, invoking Limits Tag 09MT and Cohomology of Schemes Tag 0D2N.

proof.text: Set $U=b_i^{-1}(V_i)$. It is open and contains $x$. The projection $b_i$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]; since $V_i$ is affine, $U$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2). The projection $a_i$ is also affine by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. The commuting equation $f_i a_i=b_i f$ gives $f^{-1}(U)=a_i^{-1}(f_i^{-1}(V_i))$. Hence $a_i$ restricts to an affine morphism $a:Y_U\to f_i^{-1}(V_i)$ by base-change stability [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1). Pull back the ample module of Step 5 along $a$ using [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible]. By the pullback composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] and the isomorphism of Step 3, this pullback is $\mathcal M|_{Y_U}$. It is ample by [lem-sc-ample-iso]. Its absolute ampleness includes quasi-compactness of $Y_U$ by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 0D2S, final paragraph; this uses the affine projections directly on inverse images of an affine $V_i$, without a Cartesian approximation assumption.

proof.text: For any affine open $W\subseteq U$, the inclusion $W\to U$ is a morphism between affine schemes, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Its base change $Y_W\to Y_U$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] to the ample $\mathcal M|_{Y_U}$ of Step 6. Its pullback is $\mathcal M|_{Y_W}$ by [def-pc-module-pullback], and [lem-sc-ample-iso] gives ampleness. This proves ampleness over every affine open of $U$, together with the quasi-compactness of $f^{-1}(U)$ already obtained.

source.place: Tag 0D2S, final hints; Morphisms Tags 01SH and 0892 (affine pullback).

proof_origin.place: Tag 0D2S, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood, proof. After choosing affine V_i, its final hints are implemented directly by restricting the affine limit projections and then pulling back along affine opens of U.
